text: One autumn day. <break time="0.8s" /> I called on my friend Sherlock Holmes. <break time="0.8s" /> And found him deep in conversation. <break time="0.8s" /> With a stout, elderly gentleman. <break time="0.8s" /> With fiery red hair. <break time="0.8s" /> The visitor, Mister Jabez Wilson. <break time="0.8s" /> Was a pawnbroker. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had come to Holmes. <break time="0.8s" /> With a story. <break time="0.8s" /> That was very strange indeed. <break time="0.8s" /> Holmes glanced at him. <break time="0.8s" /> And said that apart from a few obvious facts. <break time="0.8s" /> He could tell nothing about the man. <break time="0.8s" /> He has done hard work with his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> He has been in China. <break time="0.8s" /> And he has done much writing lately. <break time="0.8s" /> He added. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Wilson was astonished at first. <break time="0.8s" /> But when Holmes explained each clue. <break time="0.8s" /> He laughed and said. <break time="0.8s" /> It was nothing clever after all. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he spread an old newspaper. <break time="0.8s" /> On his knee. <break time="0.8s" /> And pointed to a strange advertisement. <break time="0.8s" /> For the Red Headed League. <break time="0.8s" /> It said that the League had a job open. <break time="0.8s" /> For a red headed man. <break time="0.8s" /> With a pay of four pounds a week. <break time="0.8s" /> For very little work. <break time="0.8s" /> Mister Wilson explained that he kept a small pawnshop. <break time="0.8s" /> In Saxe Coburg Square. <break time="0.8s" /> A quiet corner of the City of London. <break time="0.8s" /> His assistant, Vincent Spaulding. <break time="0.8s" /> Worked for only half the usual wages. <break time="0.8s" /> And he was the one. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had shown him the advertisement. <break time="0.8s" /> Spaulding had one fault. <break time="0.8s" /> For he was always running down. <break time="0.8s" /> Into the cellar. <break time="0.8s" /> To develop his photographs. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a rabbit into its hole.
